content.value_statement: Molecular ML work often slows down when teams need to choose, configure, and compare featurizers. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code build molfeat workflows for fingerprints, descriptors, pretrained embeddings, QSAR models, and virtual screening.
actual_capabilities: Recommends molfeat calculators for ECFP, MACCS, MAP4, RDKit descriptors, Mordred descriptors, and pharmacophore features.
Builds batch featurization workflows with MoleculeTransformer, parallel processing, error handling, and reproducible configuration files.
Guides pretrained molecular embedding use with ChemBERTa, ChemGPT, GIN, and Graphormer model options.
Shows how to integrate molfeat outputs with scikit-learn pipelines for QSAR, classification, and regression tasks.
Provides examples for virtual screening, similarity search, featurizer comparison, and large dataset processing.
limitations: Does not verify biological activity, assay quality, or model validity by itself.
Requires the user environment to install molfeat, RDKit, and optional model dependencies.
Pretrained model behavior depends on external packages and available compute resources.
Example workflows need domain review before use in regulated research decisions.

use_cases.title: Create QSAR Feature Pipelines
use_cases.description: Build reproducible molfeat configurations for fingerprints or descriptors before training property prediction models.

use_cases.title: Screen Compound Libraries
use_cases.description: Prepare molecular features, rank candidate compounds, and compare fast fingerprint choices for screening runs.

use_cases.title: Compare Molecular Embeddings
use_cases.description: Evaluate classical descriptors against pretrained ChemBERTa, ChemGPT, GIN, or Graphormer representations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Featurizer
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small molecular dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have SMILES strings for a QSAR baseline. Recommend a molfeat featurizer and explain the main tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Batch Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow with parallel processing and error handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a molfeat batch featurization plan for 50,000 SMILES with invalid molecule handling and reproducible configuration files.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ECFP, MACCS, RDKit descriptors, Mordred, and ChemBERTa for my regression task. Include validation and runtime considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Design Screening Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a virtual screening workflow with molfeat. Compare ECFP, MAP4, and ChemBERTa, then define evaluation metrics and caching strategy.

output_examples.input: A user asks which molfeat representation to use for a fast QSAR baseline.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends ECFP as a first baseline, explains radius and size choices, and notes when descriptors or pretrained embeddings may help.

output_examples.input: A user needs to process a large SMILES file with occasional invalid molecules.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines batch processing, parallel jobs, invalid molecule handling, and configuration saving for reproducible feature generation.

output_examples.input: A user wants to evaluate ChemBERTa features against classical fingerprints.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a comparison plan with consistent splits, runtime tracking, model caching, and metrics suited to the prediction task.

best_practices: Start with fast fingerprints before adding slower pretrained embeddings.
Save featurizer configurations and dependency versions for reproducible experiments.
Validate molecular inputs and track failed SMILES before training models.
anti_patterns: Do not compare featurizers on different train and test splits.
Do not ignore invalid molecules without recording how many failed.
Do not use expensive pretrained models before testing a simple baseline.

faq.question: What is molfeat used for?
faq.answer: It converts molecular structures into numerical features for machine learning and cheminformatics workflows.

faq.question: Can this skill help with QSAR models?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers feature selection, batch featurization, and scikit-learn pipeline integration for QSAR tasks.

faq.question: Does it support pretrained molecular models?
faq.answer: Yes. It references ChemBERTa, ChemGPT, GIN, Graphormer, and other pretrained molfeat transformers.

faq.question: Does the skill run molfeat automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users apply in their own Python environment.

faq.question: What inputs does molfeat usually need?
faq.answer: Most workflows use SMILES strings or RDKit molecule objects as inputs.

faq.question: Is this enough for regulated model decisions?
faq.answer: No. Scientific validation, data governance, and expert review are still required.
